standard_prerequisites.name: W-type rules
standard_prerequisites.statement: Formation, introduction, elimination and a propositional computation rule for W-types, the computation rule asking only for a path rather than a judgemental equality.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two rule systems that the theorem compares at source lines 700-701.

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy-initial algebra
standard_prerequisites.statement: An algebra is homotopy-initial when for every other algebra the type of homomorphisms out of it is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis of the converse direction and the source of the homomorphism used at source lines 714-715.

standard_prerequisites.name: Transport in a family of types
standard_prerequisites.statement: A path in the index type of a family induces a map between the fibres by transport, which is natural with respect to the operations of the family.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what defines the recursor at source lines 729-737 and what the final calculation consumes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sigma types and projections
standard_prerequisites.statement: The elements of a Sigma type are pairs, and the first projection forgets the second component.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the construction of the type C at source line 713 and of the composite at source lines 716-727.

core_obligations: For the forward direction, inspect the retained proof of the preceding homotopy-initiality theorem and record that only the propositional computation rule was used there (source line 707).
For the converse, assume that the polynomial functor associated to A and B has a homotopy-initial algebra (W,s_W) and show that W satisfies the propositional W-type rules (source lines 708-709).
Introduction: for a : A and t : B(a) to W define the constructor to be the structure map applied to the pair (a,t) (source lines 710-711).

Elimination: given a family C-prime over W and its premisses, equip the Sigma type C of pairs (w, c) with c in C-prime(w) with a structure map, apply homotopy-initiality to obtain a homomorphism from (W,s_W) to (C,s_C), observe that the first projection is also a homomorphism, and use contractibility of the type of endohomomorphisms to obtain an identity between the composite of the two and the identity homomorphism, in particular an identity from the composite of the first projection with the map to the identity map of W (source lines 712-727).

Define the recursor on w by transporting the second component of the map along that identity in the family sending u to the composite of C-prime with u, and verify the propositional computation rule by a calculation using the naturality of those transports (source lines 729-739).

proof_roadmap.step: Record that homotopy-initiality needs only the propositional computation rule and set up the converse.
Read off the introduction rule from the structure map.
Build the type of pairs, obtain the homomorphism by homotopy-initiality, and identify the projection composite with the identity.
Define the recursor by transport and verify the computation rule.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled theorem at source lines 700-702, printed as Theorem 5.5.5: a type satisfies the formation, introduction, elimination and propositional computation rules for W-types exactly when it is a homotopy-initial W-algebra. The author's proof (source lines 705-740) supplies the converse of the preceding homotopy-initiality theorem and does not merely cite it. Assuming that the polynomial functor has a homotopy-initial algebra (W,s_W), the elimination rule is obtained by equipping the Sigma type of pairs (w, c) with c in the assigned family over w with a structure map and applying homotopy-initiality to get a homomorphism whose composite with the first projection must be identified with the identity homomorphism, because the type of endohomomorphisms is contractible; the diagram of that composite is printed in the retained proof (source lines 712-727). The recursor itself is then manufactured by transporting the second component of that homomorphism along the resulting identity in a family of types depending on a function (source lines 729-737), and the computation rule is verified by a calculation with the naturality of those transports (source lines 738-739). The statement indicates neither that the recursor has to be built by transport nor that contractibility of the endohomomorphism type is what makes the two homomorphisms equal.
